After clearing some misconceptions of mine, I was able to find an argument. Unlike the case of abelian varieties over algebraically closed fields, polarizations of abelian schemes over an arbitrary base need not be induced from line bundles (they are after some étale base change). No line bundle implies no means of defining a canonical theta divisor on the abelian scheme. Bad news.

Fortunately, there is another path to recovering a canonical divisor from a principally polarized abelian scheme (A→S,λ)$(A \to S, \lambda)$. Although λ\lambda $\lambda$ need not come from a (relatively ample) line bundle over A A$A$, it does come from such an invertible sheaf over a torsor under A A$A$ (more precisely, under the dual scheme A∨{A}^{\vee }$A^{\vee}$, which is isomorphic to A A$A$ using λ\lambda $\lambda$). Let P P$P$ denote such a torsor (its identity will be revealed below) and L\mathcal{L}$\mathcal{L}$ some line bundle inducing λ\lambda $\lambda$ on A A$A$, then one shows that the (relative) linear system attached to L\mathcal{L}$\mathcal{L}$ is a point, so that there is a canonically defined effective divisor on P P$P$, which is the sought-after theta divisor.

Going stacky, these constructions can be carried out at the level of the universal principally polarized abelian scheme (A→A g,λ)$(A \to \mathscr{A}_g, \lambda)$, so as to define the universal torsor P i c λ A/A g{\mathrm{P}\mathrm{i}\mathrm{c}}_{A/{\mathcal{A}}_{g}}^{\lambda }$\mathrm{Pic}_{A/\mathscr{A}_g}^{\lambda}$ and a universal Theta divisor Θ\mathrm{\Theta }$\Theta$ on it. For g=2$g=2$, the relative curve Θ→A 2$\Theta \to \mathscr{A}_2$ defines a relative stable curve over A 2{\mathcal{A}}_{2}$\mathscr{A}_2$, and it follows from 2-Yoneda that there is an induced functor

Note: here we use crucially that the polarization is principal. Were it not, it could happen that there is no torsor under A A$A$ with a line bundle inducing λ\lambda $\lambda$; see Laga's preprint "Polarizations, torsors and theta groups", Theorem C.

In SGA 2, Grothendieck conjectures that the étale fundamental group of the punctured spectrum of a complete noetherian local domain of dimension at least two with algebraically closed residue field is topologically finitely generated.
## Abstract

In SGA 2, Grothendieck conjectures that the étale fundamental group of the punctured spectrum of a complete noetherian local domain of dimension at least two with algebraically closed residue field is topologically finitely generated. In this paper, we prove a weaker statement, namely that the maximal pro-nilpotent quotient of the fundamental group is topologically finitely generated. The proof uses p-adic nearby cycles and negative definiteness of intersection pairings over resolutions of singularities as well as some analysis of Lie algebras of certain algebraic group structures on deformation cohomology.
## Introduction

In SGA 2 [8], Grothendieck makes the following conjecture:

Conjecture 1.1 [8, Exposé XIII, Conjecture 3.1]

Let A be a complete noetherian local ring with algebraically closed residue field F and maximal ideal \mathfrak{m}. Let p be the characteristic of F if it is positive and let otherwise. Assume that the irreducible components of Spec A have dimension ≥2 and the scheme is connected. Then:

  * (1)

The étale fundamental group is topologically finitely generated.

  * (2)

The maximal pro-prime-to-p quotient of is topologically finitely presented.

This conjecture is in part based on Mumford's earlier study [15] in the complex-analytic setting, where a topological analogue of is shown to be finitely presented when the exceptional divisor of a resolution of singularities of A is simply connected (see [15, Section I, pp. 11–12]). Statement (2) is proved by Grothendieck-Murre [7, Theorem 9.2] when A is two-dimensional. Our focus in this paper is the pro-p part and hence Statement (1).

Grothendieck originally stated (1) in his letter to Serre dated October 1, 1961 [3], where Serre's editorial note (in 2000) reads: “I do not know whether any progress has been made on it since.” Known results indeed seem quite scarce: the only one the author could find (at the time this paper was submitted) is the work of Carvajal-Rojas-Schwede-Tucker [2], which proves that is finite of order prime to p for the case where A is a strongly F-regular singularity in equal characteristic . (But see below about the work of Hartshorne-Speiser [9].) On the other hand, wild quotient singularities constructed by Artin [1], Lorenzini [12, Corollary 6.14] and others give concrete examples with .

In this paper, we prove a weaker version of Statement (1) with no additional assumption on A:

Theorem 1.2

Under the assumptions of Conjecture 1.1, the maximal pro-nilpotent quotient of is topologically finitely generated.

In particular, the maximal abelian quotient and the maximal pro-p quotient are both topologically finitely generated.

This theorem has an application to the author's work [21] on arithmetic duality for A when A is normal and two-dimensional and has mixed characteristic. In this work, the “arithmetic cohomology” is given a canonical structure as an ind-pro-algebraic group over the residue field. Using Theorem 1.2 above, we can show (done in the subsequent work [20]) that this ind-pro-algebraic group structure actually has no connected part (that is, it is an étale group) when and . For other values of q and r, the connected part of this arithmetic cohomology may be non-trivial. For example, for and , it is closely related to Lipman's group scheme structure [11] on the Picard group of a resolution of the singularity of A. Thus the étaleness of the algebraic structure in the case and is a non-trivial finiteness statement.

Lefschetz for Local Picard groups
[Lefschetz pour les groupes de Picard locaux]

Bhatt, Bhargav ; de Jong, Aise Johan

Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure, Série 4, Tome 47 (2014) no. 4, pp. 833-849

We prove a strengthening of the Grothendieck-Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for local Picard groups conjectured by Kollár. Our approach, which relies on acyclicity results for absolute integral closures, also leads to a restriction theorem for higher rank bundles on projective varieties in positive characteristic.

Nous prouvons un renforcement du théorème de l'hyperplan de Grothendieck-Lefschetz pour les groupes locaux de Picard conjecturés par Kollár. Notre approche, qui s'appuie sur des résultats en fermetures absolues, conduit également à un théorème de restriction pour les faisceaux de rang supérieur sur les variétés projectives en caractéristique positive.
